summary.text: A 36-year-old Caucasian Portuguese male with a history of chronic alcohol abuse was admitted in October 2010 with fever (38°C), pallor, weakness and jaundice. Examination showed hepatosplenomegaly without palpable superficial lymph nodes. Blood counts showed pancytopenia, serum LDH was markedly increased at 2815 IU/L, liver tests were abnormal and coagulation tests were normal. Abdominal CT confirmed hepatosplenomegaly.

Bone marrow aspirate showed more than 80% immature cells and acute leukemia was the first hypothesis. Flow cytometry showed neoplastic cells negative for CD56 and surface CD3; the biopsy was EBER positive, the karyotype was complex, and whole blood EBV load was 57 × 10^(5) copies/ml. HIV, hepatitis B and C and HTLV markers were negative and CNS involvement was not evaluated. The final diagnosis was EBV-positive aggressive NK cell leukemia, Ann Arbor stage IVB, high risk NKIPI, ECOG status 4.

He received GEM-P (gemcitabine, cisplatin, methylprednisolone) every 28 days. The first bone marrow reevaluation on day 23 showed 0.5% abnormal NK cells and a normal karyotype, with lower EBV load and improvement in clinical status and blood counts. After the second GEM-P the aspirate showed 0.09% neoplastic NK cells, but the karyotype was again abnormal and the EBV load rose to 42 × 10^(5) copies/ml. Because of refractoriness to GEM-P, a change of chemotherapy was decided.

Nearly one month later he was admitted with loss of vision, almost total bilateral decline in visual acuity, right retinal detachment and impaired right eye abduction; head CT showed right optic nerve thickening. Five days later he developed dysphonia, dysphagia, impaired left eye abduction and left ptosis, with multiple cranial nerve palsies. CSF showed 262 cells/μl with 88% atypical mononuclear cells, consistent with leukemic meningitis. No further chemotherapy was given, best supportive care followed, and he died 107 days after the diagnosis.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.
Discussion and literature sentences about other ANKL/ENKTL cohorts are background and not patient facts.
Liver and spleen axes are printed in cm (Figure 1(a) overlays end in "mm") and kept as printed, review_only; LDH 429 versus 1587 IU/L at the urgent admission is an unresolved source conflict.

Blood values after the first GEM-P and at the urgent admission carry no explicit time label; periods of fever of 38.5 degrees or more and unmet hemophagocytic syndrome criteria from the retrospective discussion are recorded without a time.
Figure 2 caption title says bone marrow cytomorphology but its body describes peripheral blood smears; flow plot percentages and karyogram labels are image content only.
Several flow cytometry results are marked data not shown in the source and are recorded only as stated.
